cohort: The study included 3,029 non-anomalous singleton newborns at term (>=37.0 weeks) categorized as Small for Gestational Age (SGA) or Appropriate for Gestational Age (AGA) based on birth weight, delivered over 15 months at a level IV center.
finding: Persistent category II fetal heart rate tracings (FHRT) were significantly more common in SGA compared to AGA neonates, but composite neonatal adverse outcomes did not differ between the groups.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean delivery for non-reassuring FHRT was similar between SGA and AGA groups.
birth_weight: Small for Gestational Age (SGA) <10% for GA; Appropriate for Gestational Age (AGA) 10-89% for GA
